classification.difficultyReason: Apply the explicitly requested auxiliary-angle method, select both restricted-domain solutions and round only the final angles.

content.prompt: Solve each equation, for $0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ$, by transforming the LHS into a single-term sine or cosine function. Give solutions correct to the nearest minute.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}R\cos\alpha&=3\\R\sin\alpha&=5\\R^2&=3^2+5^2=34\\R&=\sqrt{34}\\\tan\alpha&=\frac53\\\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\frac53\approx59^\circ2'\end{align*}$$
Here $\alpha$ is in quadrant I. Retain its unrounded value. Let $\beta=\sin^{-1}(\frac{4}{\sqrt{34}})$.
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{34}\sin(x+\alpha)&=4\\\sin(x+\alpha)&=\frac4{\sqrt{34}}\\x+\alpha&=180^\circ-\beta\quad\text{or}\quad360^\circ+\beta\\x&=180^\circ-\beta-\alpha\\&\quad\text{or}\quad360^\circ+\beta-\alpha\\x&\approx77^\circ39'\quad\text{or}\quad344^\circ17'\end{align*}$$
The angle $x+\alpha=\beta$ gives $x<0^\circ$ and is rejected.

$$\begin{align*}R\cos\alpha&=6\\R\sin\alpha&=5\\R^2&=6^2+5^2=61\\R&=\sqrt{61}\\\tan\alpha&=\frac56\\\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\frac56\approx39^\circ48'\end{align*}$$
Here $\alpha$ is in quadrant I. Retain its unrounded value. Let $\beta=\sin^{-1}(\frac{7}{\sqrt{61}})$.
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{61}\sin(x-\alpha)&=7\\\sin(x-\alpha)&=\frac7{\sqrt{61}}\\x-\alpha&=\beta\quad\text{or}\quad180^\circ-\beta\\x&=\alpha+\beta\quad\text{or}\quad\alpha+180^\circ-\beta\\x&\approx103^\circ29'\quad\text{or}\quad156^\circ8'\end{align*}$$
